en: n. a strong complaint or disagreement about something; an event at which people show that they disagree with something; a statement that you do not agree; v. to say or show that you disagree strongly with something
ex: Thousands of people took to the streets in protest.
數千人走上街頭抗議。

en: a. relating to the mind and how it works; relating to emotions and the way you think; relating to the study of psychology
ex: The accident left her with psychological scars.
那場意外在她心裡留下了創傷。

en: n. a person who studies the human mind and behavior; a person who treats people with mental or emotional problems
ex: The psychologist helped the child deal with anxiety.
心理學家幫助那孩子應對焦慮。

en: n. a person or company that prints and sells books, magazines or newspapers; a person who owns a newspaper
ex: The publisher plans to release the novel next spring.
出版社計畫明年春天發行這本小說。

en: vt. to follow someone in order to catch them; to try to achieve something over a long period of time; to continue to do something; vi. to follow someone or something
ex: She decided to pursue a career in medicine.
她決定追求醫學事業。

en: n. the act of chasing someone or something in order to catch them; the act of trying to achieve something; an activity that you do for pleasure or as a job
ex: The police are in pursuit of the stolen car.
警方正在追捕那輛失竊的車。

en: n. an angry argument between people, usually about something unimportant; a disagreement between friends or family; vi. to argue angrily; to find fault with something
ex: The two sisters had a quarrel over a toy.
兩姊妹為了一個玩具吵架。

en: n. the amount of rain that falls in a particular place during a particular period; rain falling in an area
ex: The region has an annual rainfall of two hundred centimeters.
這個地區的年降雨量是兩百公分。

en: n. public praise or thanks for what someone has done; the act of knowing someone or something from having seen them before; the acceptance that something is true or exists; the ability of a computer to recognize voices or text
ex: She received an award in recognition of her work.
她獲頒獎項以表彰她的工作。

en: n. the process of becoming well again after an illness or injury; the act of getting back something that was lost; the process of getting better after a difficult period
ex: She made a quick recovery after her operation.
她手術後很快就復原了。

en: n. an activity that you do for enjoyment when you are not working; the enjoyment of free time; the act of creating something again
ex: The park offers many recreation activities for families.
這座公園為家庭提供許多休閒活動。

en: n. a mention of something; a letter or statement about someone's character or ability; a book or source of information; an act of looking at something for information; vt. to provide a source of information; to mention something
ex: I'm writing this letter with reference to your advertisement.
我是針對你們的廣告寫這封信。

en: n. an image that you can see in a mirror or on a shiny surface; careful thought about something; an expression of an opinion; a sign of the condition of something; criticism
ex: She saw her reflection in the window.
她在窗戶上看見自己的倒影。

en: prep. about; concerning; in connection with something
ex: I have a question regarding the exam schedule.
我有一個關於考試時間表的問題。

en: n. the act of putting your name on an official list; the process of recording information about something; the act of officially recording something such as a birth or a car
ex: Online registration for the course begins next week.
課程線上報名將於下週開始。

en: vt. to control something by making rules; to adjust something so that it works correctly; to control the amount or speed of something
ex: The government regulates the sale of medicine.
政府管制藥品的銷售。

en: n. an official rule or law; the control of something by rules; the act of adjusting something so that it works correctly
ex: Safety regulations require everyone to wear a helmet.
安全規定要求每個人都戴安全帽。

en: a. directly connected with the subject being discussed; important or useful to what is happening; suitable for a particular situation
ex: Please attach any relevant documents to your application.
請在申請書中附上任何相關文件。

en: a. not willing to do something and therefore slow to do it; showing that you do not want to do something; hesitant
ex: She was reluctant to speak in front of so many people.
她不願在這麼多人面前說話。

en: n. a comment or statement you make about something; the act of noticing something; vt. to say or write something as a comment; to notice something; vi. to say something about someone or something
ex: He made a rude remark about her clothes.
他對她的衣服說了一句不禮貌的話。

en: n. the way in which someone or something is shown or described; the act of acting or speaking for someone; a picture or model of someone or something; the group of people who represent someone
ex: The film's representation of the war was very realistic.
電影對戰爭的呈現非常寫實。

en: vt. to save someone or something from a dangerous or harmful situation; to free someone who is trapped; n. the act of saving someone or something from danger
ex: Firefighters rescued three people from the burning building.
消防員從燃燒的大樓中救出了三個人。

en: n. a person whose job is to study a subject in detail in order to discover new facts
ex: The researchers published their findings in a science journal.
研究人員在科學期刊上發表了他們的研究結果。

en: vt. to look like or be similar to someone or something
ex: She resembles her mother in many ways.
她在許多方面都像她母親。

en: n. an arrangement to keep something such as a room for you in advance; a doubt about something; a limit or condition; an area of land kept for a particular group of people
ex: I made a reservation for four at the restaurant.
我在餐廳訂了四人桌位。

en: n. a firm decision to do something; the ability to continue doing something even though it is difficult; a formal decision made by a group; the solution to a problem; the level of detail in an image on a screen
ex: She made a New Year's resolution to exercise more.
她立下新年新希望，要多運動。

en: vt. to find a solution to a problem or difficulty; to decide something firmly; to settle an argument; vi. to make a firm decision; n. a firm decision to do something
ex: They managed to resolve the dispute peacefully.
他們設法和平解決了爭端。

en: vt. to bring something back to its original condition; to give back something that was taken; to repair something such as a building or painting; to bring back a rule or practice; vi. to return to a former condition
ex: The workers restored the old church to its original appearance.
工人們把舊教堂修復成原來的模樣。

en: n. a rule or law that limits what you can do; the act of limiting something; something that prevents you from doing something
ex: There are strict restrictions on the use of mobile phones.
手機使用有嚴格的限制。

en: vt. to continue to have something; to keep something in a particular place; to remember information; to hire someone by paying them in advance
ex: The fabric retains its color even after many washes.
這種布料洗了很多次後仍然保持顏色。

en: vi. to stop working because you have reached a certain age; to go to bed; to move away from a place; vt. to make someone stop working; n. (retirement) the period after you stop working
ex: He plans to retire at the age of sixty-five.
他打算六十五歲退休。

en: vi. to move away from a place or person, especially in defeat; to change your mind; n. a quiet place where you go to rest; a move away from a place; the act of withdrawing from a difficult situation; vt. to move something back
ex: The army was forced to retreat after heavy losses.
軍隊在重大損失後被迫撤退。

en: n. a meeting of people who have not seen each other for a long time; the act of coming together again; the act of becoming friends again
ex: The class held a reunion twenty years after graduation.
班上在畢業二十年後舉辦了同學會。

en: n. a sudden and complete change in the way people do something; the act of overthrowing a government by force; the movement of an object around another; one complete circle
ex: The French Revolution changed the course of history.
法國大革命改變了歷史的進程。

en: n. something that you are given because you have done something good; money offered for finding someone or something; a feeling of satisfaction; vt. to give someone something because they have done something good
ex: A reward of a thousand dollars is offered for the missing dog.
找到那隻走失的狗，懸賞一千美元。

en: n. a word that ends with the same sound as another word; a short poem or a poem with lines that end with similar sounds; the use of such sounds in poetry; vi. (of words) to have the same ending sound; vt. to make words that end with the same sound
ex: The word "cat" rhymes with "hat".
「cat」這個字與「hat」押韻。

en: n. a strong regular pattern of sounds or movements; a regular pattern of events that happens again and again; the pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in poetry; the way something regularly moves or works
ex: The dancers moved to the rhythm of the music.
舞者隨著音樂的節奏舞動。

en: n. a question that is difficult to answer and that is asked as a game; something that is hard to understand; a large sieve; vt. to fill something with holes; vi. to ask a riddle
ex: The children enjoyed guessing the riddle.
孩子們喜歡猜謎語。

en: n. the state of being destroyed or very badly damaged; a building that has been badly damaged; the cause of someone's failure; vt. to destroy something or spoil it completely; to cause someone financial ruin; vi. to become damaged or destroyed
ex: The old castle is now a ruin.
那座古堡現已成了廢墟。

en: a. covered with rust; (of a skill) not as good as it was because you have not used it for a long time; stiff; having a reddish-brown color
ex: The old bicycle was rusty and needed a lot of oil.
那輛舊腳踏車生鏽了，需要很多潤滑油。
